title: Geometrically Constrained Learning II: Agnostic Proper Learning of Lipschitz Functions
abstract: arXiv:2611.27700v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We give a proper learner for Lipschitz functions over the Gaussian distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Given random Gaussian examples labeled by a $\lambda$-Lipschitz function, $\lambda \ge 1$, the learner returns a function $h:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ that is globally $\lambda$-Lipschitz and has loss (absolute or squared) at most $\varepsilon$. The sample complexity, running time, and representation size are \[   (d+1)^{\mathsf{poly}(\lambda/\varepsilon)}. \] The learning algorithm can be made \emph{agnostic}, given a known bound on the variance of the label marginal distribution. Some known control of label scale is information-theoretically necessary. For arbitrary labels with variance at most $V^2 \ge 1$, the complexity is \[   (d+1)^{\mathsf{poly}(V\lambda/\varepsilon)}, \] and the error is $\mathsf{opt} + \varepsilon$, where $\mathsf{opt}$ is the minimal error among Lipschitz approximators. translated_title: 几何约束学习 II：Lipschitz 函数的不可知正常学习
translated_abstract: 我们在 $\mathbb{R}^d$ 上高斯分布的背景下，给出了针对 Lipschitz 函数的一个正常学习器。给定由某个 $\lambda$-Lipschitz 函数（$\lambda \ge 1$）标注的随机高斯样本，该学习器返回一个全局满足 $\lambda$-Lipschitz 条件的函数 $h:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$，其损失（绝对损失或平方损失）至多为 $\varepsilon$。其样本复杂度、运行时间和表示规模均为 $(d+1)^{\mathsf{poly}(\lambda/\varepsilon)}$。在已知标签边缘分布方差上界的前提下，该学习算法可以成为不可知学习算法。从信息论角度看，对标签尺度的某种已知控制是必要的。对于方差不超过 $V^2 \ge 1$ 的任意标签，复杂度为 $(d+1)^{\mathsf{poly}(V\lambda/\varepsilon)}$，误差为 $\mathsf{opt} + \varepsilon$，其中 $\mathsf{opt}$ 是所有 Lipschitz 逼近器所能达到的最小误差。我们的方法结合了 $L_1$ 多项式回归……
tldr: 本文为高斯分布下的 $\lambda$-Lipschitz 函数给出了一个正常学习器，其样本复杂度、运行时间和表示规模均为 $(d+1)^{\mathsf{poly}(\lambda/\varepsilon)}$，并在已知标签方差上界时可扩展为误差为 $\mathsf{opt}+\varepsilon$ 的不可知学习算法。
en_tdlr: This paper gives a proper learner for Lipschitz functions over the Gaussian distribution with sample complexity, running time, and representation size $(d+1)^{\mathsf{poly}(\lambda/\varepsilon)}$, which can be made agnostic with error $\mathsf{opt}+\varepsilon$ given a known bound on the label variance.
